The problem, the analysis, and what it changed

Data analysis, dashboards, and machine learning where it earns its place — with the receipts.

Featured · Business Intelligence · Power BI

Sales Performance Dashboard

Business problem: four years of U.S. retail orders (2015–2018) sat in a flat file — no single screen answered what sells, to whom, and how fast it ships. Analysis: cleaned 9,800 rows into a star schema, wrote DAX measures for five core KPIs, and built one interactive Power BI page where Year, Segment, Category and Region slicers drive every visual.

  • $2.26M total sales, 4,922 orders, 793 customers, $459.48 average order value, 3.96 average shipping days.
  • Technology is the top category, Phones the top sub-category, and Consumer contributes 50.76% of sales.

How I approached it: I started from the decisions a sales lead actually makes — which category to push, which segment to protect, whether delivery is slipping — and built only the visuals that answer them. The Key insight panel states the answer in plain words, so a manager knows the next move in ten seconds, without decoding a chart.

Graduation research · ML + IoT

Predictive Smart Wearable for Hajj Pilgrim Health

Business/real-world problem: group leaders at Hajj often learn about a pilgrim's medical emergency too late, in crowds where every minute counts. Analysis: an ESP32 IoT bracelet tracking health and crowd conditions, paired with a classification model trained to flag risk early.

  • MAX30102 + MPU-6050 sensors over BLE Mesh and LoRaWAN; trained on a 60,000-record wearable health dataset.
  • Random Forest + SMOTE, corrected from 99.4% to an honest 98% after I found and fixed data leakage.

Value: prototyped down to a Group Leader Dashboard — live pilgrim status counts, location map, heart-rate trend, and an Emergency/Warning/Safe alert feed group leaders could actually act on. Targeting MDPI Sensors / Applied Sciences (Q1), supervised by Prof. Mahmoud Shams.

Business Intelligence · Power BI

IMDb Top 250 Movies Dashboard

Question: what do the best-rated films have in common, and does quality translate into money? Analysis: an interactive Power BI report on the IMDb Top 250, with Release Year, IMDb Rating and Genre slicers driving every visual.

  • 250 movies, $51.7bn total gross, 8.31 average rating, 129-minute average duration, 54 high-rated titles (21.6%).
  • Crime is the top-rated genre (8.40), Action brings 45% of gross, R is the most common certificate (97 films, 39%), and the Russo brothers lead directors at $4.85bn.

Why it stands out: it doesn't just rank films, it tests whether quality pays. Ratings barely differ between genres, but revenue is concentrated in a few — and the Key Insights panel recalculates that story for any filter you choose.

power bidaxdata storytelling
DEPI Project 1 · Data analysis

Humanitarian population data pipeline

Business problem: raw displacement survey data across Iraq, Libya, Syria, and Yemen is too messy and incomplete for planners to use as-is. Analysis: a six-step Python pipeline — import, cleaning, feature engineering, aggregation, scaling, and visualization — from raw import to a published finding.

  • ~9,917 records cleaned to 100% completeness; four engineered features (Male %, Female %, Avg. People per House, Dominant Housing).
  • MinMax and Z-score scaling, zero statistical outliers (|Z| > 3).

Insight → value: Room, Flat, and House correlate almost perfectly with each other but strongly negatively with Tent — a fast, data-backed way to read how far a camp has shifted toward permanent housing, instead of reading it off a raw survey export. Published as an 11-slide LinkedIn carousel.

How I think about data: I start with the question — where is need concentrated, how fast is it changing, what housing exists? — then merge and clean the raw files in Python, because every number downstream depends on that step. I rebuild the key totals in Excel PivotTables to cross-check the Python results, and only then publish dashboards (Excel and Power BI) that lead with the decision, not the chart. Two tools agreeing is what lets you trust the 59.01M, Yemen's 40.61% share, and the 4.24% drop.

Experiments · Applied AI · Amazon PartyRock

PartyRock apps

Data analysis app: an AI assistant over a body-measurement dataset (2,018 subjects, 14 measurements) that returns summary statistics, correlations and body-proportion ratios from plain-language questions, for example a 0.927 chest–waist correlation. Hormonal Health Guide: takes an age and a list of symptoms and generates a plain-language explanation plus daily wellness advice.

Why it matters: two working generative-AI apps, shipped without a backend — one turns a plain-language question into analysis, the other turns a personal input into tailored guidance. The health app states clearly that it is general wellness support, not a diagnosis.

partyrockapplied aiprompt design
Applied ML

Blood donor prediction

Business problem: blood banks can't call every past donor — they need a way to prioritize outreach toward the people most likely to actually come back. Analysis: an Arabic-language Streamlit app predicting whether a donor is likely to donate again soon, from their donation history.

  • Inputs: recency, frequency, total volume donated, and time since first donation (the classic RFM blood-donation dataset).
  • Trained scikit-learn classifier with a saved scaler, served through a Streamlit UI.
